introduction: “The Lord, peerless is He, hath made woman and man to abide with each other in the closest companionship, and to be even as a single soul.” These readings describe marriage as a means of spiritual progress: husband and wife are to know each other’s character, be faithful, consult, give way to each other, and help each other’s spiritual life; such a union, the readings say, outlasts death, whereas one that is only physical ends with it. Genesis, the Song of Songs, Ecclesiastes’ “two are better than one”, the Qur’an’s “love and mercy”, the prayer of Tobias and the working partnership of Priscilla and Aquila are the nearest company. Jesus’s saying that in the resurrection “they neither marry” and Paul’s worry that the married are distracted are the contrary voices from within scripture. Plato’s myth of the other half is the idea of the soul mate that reading 44 sets aside, and Gibran’s “spaces in your togetherness” asks what “a single soul” should not mean.
questions: The readings call for husband and wife to be “even as a single soul” and also to consult, which assumes two minds. How do you put these together? Does Gibran help?
Reading 10 distinguishes a marriage that death ends from one that endures. What makes the difference, according to the readings?
Paul feared that marriage divides a person’s attention; reading 32 says one can marry and serve. What would a marriage look like that proved Paul wrong? Consider Priscilla and Aquila.
Reading 31 warns against either spouse adoring the other “instead of God”. What does that danger look like in ordinary life?
Reading 44 says there are no “soul mates”. What is lost, and what gained, by giving up that idea?

outside.why: Become thoroughly acquainted with each other’s character before the covenant. Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?
A bond meant to be “a firm and everlasting” one. Shakespeare: let me not to the marriage of true minds admit impediments. Love is not love which alters when it alteration finds.
Woman and man made to abide in the closest companionship, “even as a single soul”. This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.
Two are better than one; for if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy.

A husband’s studies and a wife’s wish to serve abroad, to be settled by consulting. Aquila and Priscilla worked at one trade, moved together from Rome to Corinth to Ephesus, and are always named as a pair.
Each sacrifices their right for the other. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.
The greatest bond is faithfulness and loyalty. She is thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.
Firmness and steadfastness to one’s companion and confidant. Rejoice with the wife of thy youth.
Affection that leaves others astonished. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.

A husband’s love and kindness will make him spiritual. Paul to those married to unbelievers: what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife?

Marriage among most people is a physical bond that death ends; the union of spirits endures “in all the worlds of God”. Jesus answered a question about the next life differently: in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels. Do the two disagree about what survives, or about what to call it?
Set me as a seal upon thine heart: for love is strong as death. Many waters cannot quench love.

The real relation, founded on spiritual love, is not ended by parting. Donne to his wife before a journey: our two souls therefore, which are one, endure not yet a breach, but an expansion, like gold to airy thinness beat.
Man and woman should truly be friends. Aristotle: without friends no one would choose to live, though he had all other goods.

Sympathy and understanding with a basis in reality. Gibran’s counsel to the married: let there be spaces in your togetherness, and let the winds of the heavens dance between you. The readings speak of becoming “even as a single soul”. Are these opposed, or two halves of one account?
Marry a wise and faithful person. Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing.
Do not hurry; it is better to wait. Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days.
It depends on consent. Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
“Marriage must be strict and pure.” Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.
A holy covenant into which the young should enter. A man shall leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife.
Among the laws He gave to set the world in order. It is not good that the man should be alone.
The covenant as a sign of unity and a means to salvation. Tobias on his wedding night: I take not this my sister for lust, but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.
The tie between husband and wife is the Word of God. Peter: heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.
United “even as though they were one person”. They are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

From the pairing of things come good results. Plato’s Aristophanes tells the famous myth: each of us is but the indenture of a man, always looking for his other half. Reading 44 says plainly that the Faith does not teach that “soul mates” exist. What is the difference between finding one’s other half and building “a profound friendship of spirit”?
An engagement that will “yield great results” for others. Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers, who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom all the churches give thanks.
A union outward and inward, for all one’s days. Whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge.

If a spouse prevents the other from entering the Light. The Gospel’s hardest saying on rival loyalties: if any man come to me, and hate not his wife, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
When either adores the other instead of God. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.

“Thou canst take unto thyself a husband and at the same time serve the Cause of God.” Paul doubted it: he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife. Whose experience do you recognise?
The same pair, teaching together: Aquila and Priscilla took Apollos unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
Marriage joined with spirituality. Zacharias and Elisabeth: they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments.
It is highly important to raise a family. Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord.
A young man cannot appreciate the blessings until he is older. Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine: thy children like olive plants round about thy table.
The world’s enlightenment depends on the existence of man. Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.
Children and grandchildren of goodly character are a lasting deed. Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.

Gibran reminds parents whose the children are: they come through you but not from you, and though they are with you yet they belong not to you. How does that sit with children as one’s “righteous deeds that endure”?
A wedding prayer for two birds of one nest. The Qur’an’s prayer of the faithful: our Lord! vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring.
Two birds singing on a cedar branch in remembrance of God. My beloved is mine, and I am his.
Marriage should lead to a profound friendship of spirit. Let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works.

shortfall: Readings 7, 16, 20, 25, 28, 29, 35, 37, 41 and 43 repeat points made by their neighbours in a sentence or two, or concern kinship and offspring treated in other guides; their neighbours’ companions serve for them.

And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless
